content_preview.summary: Go 1.27 extends the experimental simd/archsimd package from amd64 to arm64 and WebAssembly, replacing assembly for vector code, per a Go blog post.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Go team has published a detailed look at the architecture-specific SIMD API that ships experimentally in Go 1.27. According to the [Go blog](https://go.dev/blog/archsimd), "Since Go 1.26, we have supported an experimental `amd64` SIMD API. Now in Go 1.27, we support two more architectures: `arm64` and `wasm`." The post, written by Junyang Shao and David Chase and dated 2 October 2026, says the APIs are enabled by setting `GOEXPERIMENT=simd` at build time and live in the `simd/ar...

editor_notes.content_quality: News, 785 body words (policy range 400-1200, within range). Title is 110 characters (cap 150, within cap). Clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure; technically precise, all code identifiers match the source.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both gzipped snapshots from disk (no re-fetch); manifest shows HTTP 200 for both, suspicious_patterns null for both. source-0.html.gz (https://go.dev/blog/archsimd, 'Arch-specific SIMD in Go', Junyang Shao and David Chase, 2 October 2026, 6 days old at review): CONFIRMED. Verbatim quotes checked: 'Since Go 1.26, we have supported an experimental amd64 SIMD API. Now in Go 1.27, we support two more architectures: arm64 and wasm.' (article adds code formatting only); 'anyone who wanted to use SIMD in Go had to endure the friction of writing assembly language'; 'essentially the intrinsics layer in other languages'; 'not yet landed in Go 1.27'. Also confirmed: GOEXPERIMENT=simd and simd/archsimd package; amd64 AVX/AVX2/many AVX-512, arm64 NEON with 'SVE and some SVE2 already on the way', wasm 'mostly complete'; AMX/SME unsupported; ShiftAllLeft vs _mm512_slli_epi64; Float32x4/Int32x8/Uint8x16/Mask32x4; PermuteOrZero (amd64 VPSHUFB) vs LookupOrZero (NEON VTBL, wasm i8x16.swizzle); Grouped suffix with InterleaveLoGrouped; ToBits() and ReshapeToUint<W>s() replacing As<Type>; x.IfElse(m, y) replacing Merge; archsimd.X86.AVX512GFNI(), archsimd.ARM64.SVE(), SIGILL warning; AVX512() block fusing into merge-masked VPADD; #24416 and #73787 issue numbers; test commands GOEXPERIMENT=simd go test simd/archsimd/... and GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm; Future work: SVE/SVE2 for Go 1.28 and beyond, and riscv64, ppc64, s390x, loong64 planned, no dates. source-1.html.gz (https://go.dev/blog/simd-experiment, 'Platform-independent SIMD in Go', David Chase and Junyang Shao, 24 September 2026, 14 days old): CONFIRMED. 'Go 1.26 introduced a SIMD API for amd64, and Go 1.27 added APIs for arm64 (specifically NEON) and wasm' and 'Go 1.27 ... introduces an experimental, fully portable, platform- and size-agnostic SIMD interface' support the companion paragraph. Neither post gives benchmark figures or a date for leaving GOEXPERIMENT, so the 'What We Don't Know' items are accurate. Both posts are first-party Go project blog posts (go.dev), attributed as such in the article. No source text addressed an AI agent or contained instructions.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All claims trace to the two cited sources. Headline does not overstate: it says 'Still Behind GOEXPERIMENT=simd' and does not claim SIMD is on by default in Go 1.27. Vendor claims are attributed to the Go blog throughout. Internal link /article/2026-08/20-go-127-ships-as-stable-release-finalizing-generic-methods-and-adding-encodingjsonv2 resolves to an existing published article (singular /article/ form).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No AI self-reference. One minor wording point in the summary: 'replacing assembly for vector code' is slightly stronger than the source, which says archsimd gives users an alternative to writing assembly ('is here to change that'); it is attributed 'per a Go blog post' and is not a substantive error.
editor_notes.originality: New angle. The Go 1.27 release article (2026-08/20) mentioned the experimental simd package only in passing, and the Go 1.26 article (2026-02/05) covered the original amd64 SIMD support; this article covers the new arm64/wasm archsimd detail from the 2 October and 24 September 2026 blog posts. No duplicate found.
concerns: Summary phrase 'replacing assembly for vector code' slightly overstates the source (an alternative to writing assembly, not a replacement); minor, not worth a correction.
Freshness: both source posts are recent (6 and 14 days old); the API is explicitly experimental and has changed between Go 1.26 and 1.27, as the article states.
recommendations: Prefer 'offering an alternative to assembly' over 'replacing assembly' in future summaries.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, neutral News article. Word count (785) and title length (110) are within policy; signature and hash valid; go.dev already on the allowlist (no allowlist change). APPROVE.
